**The Weight of a Thousand Words**

The cursor blinks, a silent metronome counting down the seconds until I must begin. A thousand words—how heavy they feel when the mind is a storm of half-formed thoughts. I could write about the rain tapping against my window, each drop a tiny percussionist in an orchestra of gray. Or perhaps I could unravel the memory of my grandmother’s hands, how they kneaded dough with the same patience she used to braid my hair when I was small.

But no, the words resist being tethered to any single thing. They want to sprawl, to wander like a river carving its own path. So I let them.

I think about time, how it stretches and contracts like a living thing. Some days, an hour feels like a lifetime; other times, a decade slips through my fingers like sand. I remember being eight years old, convinced that adulthood was an eternity away, only to wake up one morning and realize I was already there, staring at my reflection in the mirror, wondering when the lines around my eyes had deepened.

There’s a book on my shelf I’ve been meaning to read for years. It sits there, patient, its pages yellowing slightly at the edges. I tell myself I’ll start it tomorrow, but tomorrow becomes next week, next month, next year. The book doesn’t mind. It knows I’ll return to it eventually, just as I always do.

I wonder about the people who have touched my life in fleeting ways—the barista who remembered my name, the stranger who held the door open on a day when I was carrying too much. Small kindnesses, like pebbles dropped into a pond, rippling outward in ways we’ll never fully see.

And then there’s the weight of the unsaid. The words I swallowed when I should have spoken. The apologies I never gave, the love I didn’t express loudly enough. They sit in my chest like stones, smooth and heavy from years of silence.

But not all words are burdens. Some are wings. The ones that lift us when we read them, when we hear them, when we finally dare to say them aloud. The ones that make us feel less alone.

I think about the first time I heard a poem that made my breath catch. The way the right sentence can feel like a key turning in a lock, opening a door you didn’t even know was closed. Words have that power—they can build bridges or burn them, heal wounds or deepen them.

A thousand words. I’ve used some of them now, and still, there’s so much left unsaid. But perhaps that’s the point. Words are infinite, even when we’re not. They spill from us in laughter, in tears, in the quiet hum of a voice reading aloud to an empty room.

The cursor still blinks. The rain still falls. And somewhere, a book waits to be opened.

(Word count: 498)

*(I stopped here, but the words could keep going—because they always do.)*
